newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand firms as long dollar positions cut.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand firms as long dollar positions cut.

text.p: The rand was at its best level in nearly four weeks in early Thursday afternoon trade as higher carry costs forced long dollar positions to bale out, dealers said.

At 1115 GMT, the rand was pegged at 4.6185/6235 against the dollar -- more than four cents better than its overnight 4.6650/6700 finish -- after earlier firming to a day's strongest level of 4.6175 bid.

Dealers said that the Reserve Bank's announcement on Wednesday that it would hike interest rates by one point to 17 percent from Thursday had made the cost of carrying long dollar positions prohibitive.

"The Reserve Bank's interest rate hike makes the cost of carry more expensive, which makes holding long dollars and short rand a costly exercise, so people are getting out of long dollar positions," Banque Indosuez trader Rudy Jordaan said.
The rand's gains were capped, however, by importers looking to buy dollars below the 4.62 level, dealers said.
Jordaan said that an important technical level to watch on the day would be the 4.6170 level, which he said was expected to hold for the time being.
